selector_result.evaluation_process: Q1 fills in the budget-usage constraint (must the $7M be fully spent or can it be left partially unused), which directly changes the feasible set and objective treatment. Q2 fills in whether at least one property must be purchased, affecting whether the empty selection is feasible. Q3 fills in the directionality/symmetry of the Property 4–Property 3 exclusion, a constraint-structure detail. All three address OPEN ledger gaps and are business-answerable. Q1 is the strongest first question because budget usage is a core hard constraint that, if left unconfirmed, would force the Agent to silently assume either full-spend or under-spend behavior; this assumption materially changes which property subsets are feasible and how the income-maximization objective is modeled. Q2 is also important but is a weaker boundary condition, and Q3 is a narrower constraint-interpretation detail. Therefore Q1 best reduces pre-modeling silent-assumption risk.

Q1 directly asks about a hard requirement on the number of properties, which is a constraint/business-rule gap and would most change the model's feasible set. Q2 asks about a management/holding limit, which is a softer operational preference and overlaps with Q1 but is less central. Q3 asks about diversification preference, which is a soft objective/tradeoff issue and less likely to be a hard constraint. Since the objective, budget, whole-property purchase, and exclusion rules are already confirmed, the highest-value remaining gap is whether any minimum/exact/maximum property-count rule exists. Q1 is clearest, mutually exclusive, and answerable by a business user, and it best reduces silent-assumption risk about the feasible decision scope.
